segments: ... was continually in wars with the Arabs.
And in the year [1287 of the Greeks], the Tigris River overflowed twenty cubits more than usual,
and water gushed out from the wells and sewers of Baghdad.
And people lived in boats night and day,
and many courtyards collapsed.
And when the two brothers became rulers over the Romans,
they appointed as Domesticus for themselves a certain man named Vardas.
And he immediately rebelled against them,
and wanted to establish a kingdom for himself over the territories which the Romans had taken from the Arabs.
And he sent his brother as an envoy to 'Adud al-Dawlah, the Emir of Baghdad, to help him,
and to take care that he be established in the kingdom of the Romans in the East,
and that he would be in subjection to the Arabs all the days of his life.
Then Basil and Constantine the kings also sent envoys,
and urged that they should not accept the words of the rebel.
'Adud al-Dawlah judged in his mind
that it was right to help kings,
and not a rebel.
Nevertheless, he showed outward affection to the rebel's brother,
and promised that he would help him in everything.
Then, when the kings of the Romans sent an army against the rebel,
he with confidence entered the border of the Arabs with a few men,
and sent to 'Adud al-Dawlah to send him an army.
And while he was putting his trust in him,
he secretly sent word to the chiefs of the Arabs,
and they seized the rebel, and his brother, and those who were with him,
and they were brought to Baghdad,
and were imprisoned there for a long time.
And in the year 1292 [of the Greeks],
372 of the Arabs,
'Adud al-Dawlah, the Emir of Baghdad, died.
In his time lived 'Ali ibn al-'Abbas the physician,
who composed the book 'al-Malaki' {OCR?} in this man's name,
because these emirs who ruled alongside the Caliph in Baghdad
were called kings.
And at this time also,
there was in Khurasan Abu Sahl al-Masihi, the distinguished physician,
who wrote the famous 'Book of the Hundred Treatises',
and he has other books as well.
And he was the master of the Elder Prince [Ibn Sina].
And at forty years of age this Masihi departed from this world.
And in his place arose Samsam al-Dawlah, his brother.
And in the year 1293 [of the Greeks],
notes: [variant: 373 of the Arabs, there was famine in Baghdad, and a kor of wheat was sold for four thousand]
